text:
Small Airports Struggle to Hold On to Routes

Regional airports across the continent are losing services as airlines concentrate their fleets on busier hubs. The trend, which began before the pandemic, has [1] since 2022, with more than forty routes withdrawn in a single year. [2] The airport at Kelburn, which served half a million passengers a decade ago, now handles fewer than a third of that number.

Local authorities have responded with subsidies, but these are [3] controversial: opponents argue that public money should not be used to support commercial carriers. Airport managers point out, [4], that a single route can sustain hundreds of jobs in surrounding communities.

questions.explanation: A trend that has 'accelerated' has speeded up; 'accumulated' means built up, 'accompanied' needs an object, and 'accredited' means officially recognized.

choices: The consequences for the airlines that depend on these airports have been minor, and in some cases reversible.
The consequences for the communities that depend on these airports have been severe, and in some cases irreversible.
The consequences for the communities that depended on these airports were severe, and in some cases irreversible.
The causes for the communities that depend on these airports have been severe, and in some cases avoidable.
questions.explanation: The next sentence gives the example of Kelburn, whose traffic has fallen sharply, so the previous one must introduce severe consequences for communities; the others mention airlines, a past tense, or causes.
'Highly controversial' is the fixed collocation; 'hardly' means scarcely and would reverse the meaning.
The managers' point contrasts with the opponents' argument; 'however' marks the contrast.

text:
Dear Members,

The Board of the Calloway Credit Union is pleased to enclose the annual report and accounts for the year ended 30 June. Total deposits rose by 8 percent, [1] lending grew by only 3 percent, reflecting the cautious approach that the Board has adopted in a period of economic uncertainty.

[2] The Board recommends a dividend of 1.5 percent, which will be paid in November subject to your approval at the annual meeting on 14 October. Members who are unable to attend are [3] to vote by post, using the form enclosed. The Board would like to [4] its thanks to the volunteers whose work has made these results possible.

Yours sincerely,
Peter Hollis
Chair

questions.explanation: 'Whereas lending grew by only 3 percent' contrasts the growth in deposits with slower lending.

choices: Despite this caution, the union has become unprofitable and has weakened its reserves for the second consecutive year.
Despite this caution, the union has remained profitable and has strengthened its reserves for the second consecutive year.
Because of this caution, the union has remained profitable and has strengthened its competitors for the second year.
Despite this ambition, the union has remained profitable and has strengthened its reserves for the first consecutive year.
questions.explanation: The next sentence recommends a dividend, which presupposes profit; the first option states it. The others say it is unprofitable, refer to competitors, or contradict 'caution' with 'ambition'.
'Are entitled to vote by post' needs the past participle after 'are'.
The Board would like to 'extend' its thanks; after 'to' a base verb is needed and 'extend' collocates with 'thanks'.
